## First-touch grading — graded `pm:queue`, routed `domain:devx`

Dispatching PM seat, session `session_f95e3874-e532-4748-a921-044aa2752a2b`, 2026-09-10T12:0xZ.

⚠️ **An execution seat is grading a `finding`, which is normally the triage seat's sole output.** The authority is the maintainer's direct instruction in this session, verbatim (⛔ quoted, not translated): 「相关任务你都派发处理完」, covering the follow-ups this chain produced. The direct-dispatch channel routes them here. Recorded so the triage seat can see why, and can override.

**Grade: `pm:queue`.** A named landing point and a named cheapest route exist (extend the existing pin that already derives `PUBLISHED_SUBPATHS` from `packages/spec/package.json`, or add a root docs gate), so there is nothing to ask before someone can act. It restores an invariant rather than widening a surface, which is the shape `pm:queue` collects.

**Route: `domain:devx`.** The SUBJECT is documentation correctness held by a gate — `content/docs/**` and gate scripts are that lane, per the lane table's split of governance-of-docs-quality into `devx`. ⚠️ Stated because it is arguable: option 1's cheapest landing point is `packages/runtime/src/spec-subpath-alias-coverage.pin.test.ts`, and `packages/runtime` belongs to `domain:cli`; option 2 would land in `packages/spec/scripts/build-docs.ts` (`domain:spec`). The dispatch tells the dev to stop and report if its chosen route lands outside `content/docs/**` plus a gate script, rather than silently crossing a lane boundary.

⭐ Type `Task` — this is the invariant the whole #16325 chain existed to restore, applied to the one surface no gate covers: every mechanical counter of the subpath set moved when `./cloud` was deleted, and all three prose enumerations stayed stale until a human sweep caught them.

Claim: PM direct maintainer dispatch (no numbered round — direct-dispatch channel)
Session: `session_f95e3874-e532-4748-a921-044aa2752a2b`
Branch: `claude/issue-17388-docs-subpath-enumerations-gated`
Worktree: `objectstack-issue-17388`
Domain: `domain:devx`
File surface: `content/docs/{deployment/troubleshooting,plugins/packages,getting-started/glossary}.mdx` · one gate script (`scripts/` or the existing `packages/runtime/src/spec-subpath-alias-coverage.pin.test.ts`) · `package.json` scripts + the CI workflow that runs the gate family it joins · `.changeset/` (stop on breach; explain in the report)
Container & model: `M`, `mode:subagent`, `model: <default judgment tier>` — ⛔ NOT the contract-review tier: this adds a gate over prose, it does not change what any published contract accepts or rejects
Clause-②: no
Serial constraints cleared: `#17383` is queued in this lane and MAY land in `packages/spec/scripts/` — same package as this card's option 2. It is held BEHIND this card rather than run beside it (fold-or-serial answered: serial, because the two share a possible package and neither is urgent enough to buy the risk). No other in-flight card declares `content/docs/**` or the runtime pin.

---

Maintainer authorisation, verbatim (⛔ quoted, not translated): 「相关任务你都派发处理完」.

### Premise at dispatch time

`origin/main` **`776d64cd3`** — the merge commit of #17372, which is what made this finding actionable. The three
pages are **correct today** (the patch round `ef1fda259` fixed them by hand); ⛔ this card is not a docs fix. It is
the gate that keeps them correct, and the dev must not mistake a green grep for nothing to do.

The measurement that motivates it, from the #17372 review: when `./cloud` left the exports map, **every mechanical
counter moved with it** — the anti-vacuity floor pin, the alias-coverage pin, `export-origins`, `root-meta`,
`llms.txt`, `quick-reference` counts, ~25 in all — and **all three prose enumerations stayed stale**, because
nothing reads them. Step 2 of that chain was FAILed in review by exactly this class of unlisted counter.

⚠️ Two sets, not one: the exports map has **16** `./*` entries (`meta-spelling` is a subpath but not a protocol
namespace); the namespace lists have **15**. A gate that conflates them will be wrong on its first run.

```

## MERGED — the gate is on `main`. `pm:dispatched` stripped in the same write.

Dispatching PM seat, 2026-09-11T00:5xZ.

**Two readings, plus a third that checks the thing actually runs.**

1. `pulls/17435` ⇒ `merged: true`, `merged_at: 2026-09-10T16:20:59Z`, merge commit `0f384078c`.
2. On the ref: `git cat-file -e origin/main:scripts/check-docs-spec-enumerations.mjs` succeeds.

Auto-close left `pm:dispatched` on a closed card — the same half-state #16450, objectui#8225 and #16325 each
left behind. Stripped; `domain:devx` stays, because ownership is not state.

### What is now held that was not held before

Five hand-written enumerations under `content/docs/**` are checked against `packages/spec/package.json`'s
`exports` map on every PR: the ordered subpath sentence in `troubleshooting.mdx`, the namespace list in
`plugins/packages.mdx`, and the glossary's namespace sentence, layers table (with its own partition and
no-duplicate rules) and per-namespace sections — plus a corpus-wide sweep of numeric namespace-count claims,
prose only.

The two sets are **derived, not typed**: 16 bare `./NAME` subpaths, and the 15 of those whose `CATEGORY_TITLES`
entry ends in `" Protocol"`. `meta-spelling` is published but is not a protocol; `conversions` and `migrations`
are protocols but are not published. Both edge cases fall out of the derivation, so the next subpath change
moves the gate with it instead of leaving prose behind.

### Why this card existed, kept here because the reason is the lesson

`#16325` deleted the `@objectstack/spec/cloud` subpath. **Every mechanical counter of that set moved with it** —
an anti-vacuity floor pin, the alias-coverage pin, `export-origins`, `root-meta`, `llms.txt`, the
quick-reference counts, around 25 in all. Each moved because something went red and pointed at it.

**All three prose enumerations stayed stale**, and were found only because a contract-review pass asked for a
sweep. One of them, `troubleshooting.mdx`, was still telling readers that `cloud` was an importable subpath on
the day the subpath stopped existing.

⇒ That chain spent three steps and three repos restoring the rule that a declaration must match what is real.
The documentation was the same defect in the one corner no gate covered. It is covered now.
